facts.text: Chestnut Mound earned its name from a prominent hill blanketed in American chestnut trees that once crowned the local landscape.
The community’s post office opened in 1855, officially recognizing Chestnut Mound as a distinct rural settlement in Smith County.
Chestnut Mound once served as the terminus of the Trousdale Ferry Pike, a stagecoach route that crossed the Caney Fork River by ferry.
Nestled on Smith County’s eastern ridge, Chestnut Mound sits between the Nashville Basin and the Highland Rim, where hills rise from river valleys.
At roughly 971 feet above sea level, Chestnut Mound’s elevation places it comfortably within the region’s rolling uplands.
Early 19th‑century settlers, mainly Scots‑Irish, English, and German from North Carolina, arrived via the Walton Road and cleared farms along the Caney Fork.
